DOP: ibha m. [ ts ], an elephant ; Abh 360; Sadd 345, 33* ; Sv-pṭ I 388, 11 ; — ifc see mattebha sv madati ; — °- pipphalī , f. [ cf S. ibhakaṇā, hastipippalī], a sort of long pepper ; Abh 583.
CPD: ibha , m. [ ts. ] , elephant; Abh 360 c (kuñjara+), Sadd 345, 33* ( among 12 words for hatthī); Mogg Vll 127 ( formation of the word ); Himālayaṃ . . . ~ -dīpi- kapīhi . . . samākulaṃ, Jina-c 24 ( among other wild animals in Sumedha legend ); — ifc. mattebha (matta + ibha), elephant in rut, Jināl 62, Dāth V 30; Setibhinda (set'-ibh'-inda), "Lord of the White Ele- phants", Npr. of various kings of Prome and Pegu (PLB index ).

ibbha.p: [Ibha+va] (ti) CL=8 Va-nhaṅa့ bha-rhe့nokaprana, vakiu ba-pru. Dhāna, ṭī.725. I+bha. Sūci. Ibha+ya. Vi,pi,dhāna.(ibhya-saṃ)]   (1) (a) A person who is rich ; he. wealthy person. (B) worth with the instigation of elephant, who has the instigation similar to elephant's; he. inferior house owner, inferior host, inferior lineage, low lineage, Suda lineage. (Pu) . (2) elephant keeper. Ibbha-(2)- see. Ibbha(ti) [ibbha+ṇa]  who similar/look like elephant keeper,  owner of house.
